newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes ease late, hurt by API stock builds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes ease late, hurt by API stock builds.

text.p: U.S. crudes pulled back in late trade Tuesday after a bearish build in crude stocks threatened to intensify fundamental pressure, traders said.
A fire at Shell's Wood River, Illinois refinery, which cut in on runs at the 268,000 barrel per day (bpd) plant, also put pressure on domestic grade differentials, traders said.
"Grades came off slightly in the after-market," a Texas trader said, noting confusion on how crude stocks nationwide built 9.3 million barrels for the week ended Nov 1.
Dec West Texas Intermediate was at $22.60-70 a barrel, down 15 cts from Monday, and off an intraday high of $23.09.
The API showed gasoline stocks rose 4.7 million barrels, which also doused the short-term bullish sentiment.
Crude prices had been supported by firm gasoline prices lately, and with such builds in stocks, traders said they expected refinery rates to drop back even further.
In domestics, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at plus 67/68 cents over WTI, down from Monday's 70 cents.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire moved at 71 cts premium, off from last Friday's trade at 74 cents.
Midland/WTI was steady at 3-5 cents above the marker, having sold earlier in the session at a weaker 2-3 cents.
Dec Postings Plus barely budged at $1.95-$1.98, bound by the unchanged levels in Dec/Jan WTI at 28-30 cents.
Sours lost some ground in late action after Shell's fire threatened to rein in operating capacity.
West Texas Sour fell to $1.60 discount to WTI/Cushing, down from the morning's minus $1.57 level.
Overall softness in European markets and no shortage of nearby foreign crudes, continued to add to the defensive posture of domestic light and heavy grades, traders said.
